title: I Built a Chess Game Where Anyone Can Create Their Own Bots Without Coding
author: Embarrassed_Text_347
selftext:
I've been working on a project called BotGambit, a chess platform where players can create, customize, and share their own chess bots without needing to write any code.

Instead of just playing against normal chess engines, you can create bots with completely different behaviors and rules. Some get stronger as the game progresses, others prioritize certain pieces, and some have mechanics that completely change how you approach a match.

One of the biggest challenges has been building a system flexible enough to support all these different behaviors while keeping the bot creator simple enough for anyone to use.

The community has already created almost 1000 bots, and I've been expanding the platform with ranked matches, daily challenges, progression systems, and events that combine multiple bot mechanics into one. We launched on iOS about two weeks ago, and on google play about a month ago. So far, iOS has been pretty slow, but google play is doing decent.

**How I've used generative AI:** I've been using AI-assisted coding tools like Codex throughout development to help implement features, work through technical problems, and iterate on ideas. It has been super helpful with taking care of the monotonous things so I can focus all my attention on the gameplay experience. 

It's been a fun project to develop, especially seeing what people come up with when they're given the tools to create their own custom chess bot opponents.

You can try it here: [https://botgambit.com](https://botgambit.com)

It's sometimes difficult to balance the freedom of users versus keeping things simple and straightforward. I'd be interested to hear what other developers think of the concept, especially how you'd approach expanding the bot creation system without overcomplicating it for users.
